messages:
jen_sales: Heads up  AtlasCare wants med-qa-7b-v2 on Private for a 4-week POC. Requirements: SentencePiece 32k, int4 quant, HSM-backed CMEK, p50 < 150ms for single-user UI. Can infra and security confirm any blockers?
ryan_se: We support med-qa family but must validate tokenizer byte-level parity. If they can attach the .spm model we can diff token ids.
alex_infra: KV-cache + int4 is the main runtime risk. I'll run a quick smoke test on a small dedicated node and compare int4 vs fp16 canary.
claire_sec: Security front: CMEK with HSM-supported KMS is OK in Private. We need to confirm contact for NDA to share SOC2 summary and that audit logs can be exported. I'll draft a one-paragraph answer.
jen_sales: Also need a POC price ballpark (infra + support hours). Can infra give a rough delta for int4 vs fp16 for Dedicated?
alex_infra: Ballpark: int4 usually reduces per-token cost by 30-45% depending on kernel maturity. Quote the quant tier and we'll refine after perf sweep.
ryan_se: Test plan I'll add: tokenizer parity, generation quality check (perplexity delta), and a small clinical prompt set fuzz. If mismatch, propose canonical tokenizer export or an fp16 canary.
ci_bot: Ticket created: RINF-9307  "AtlasCare med-qa-7b-v2 POC: tokenizer+quant+CMEK validation". Assignee: alex_infra. ETA 48h.
jen_sales: Great. I'll request their SentencePiece artifact and ask legal for NDA to share SOC2. Will update once infra posts results. :thumbsup:
